title: Roadmap
intro_md: What we're working on and what's next. No dates, since things ship when their reviews and checks pass.

items.title: Automatic handover for the GE thread
items.detail_md: An Auto mode that hands over both ways, keeping a game synchronous where the two threads would only take turns.

items.title: The screensavers redone
items.detail_md: The next part of my redesign of the app's look: its screensavers, with the CRT and XMB ones in the theme's colours.

items.title: The Android app's interface on the desktop
items.detail_md: The desktop program's interface is a placeholder for now; I want it on a par with the Android app's.

items.title: A matched N64 comparison with Mupen64Plus-AE
items.detail_md: Mario Tennis on Phobos and on the Mupen64Plus-AE build I supplied, with the same device, scene and settings, and each APK tied to its source.

items.title: Tracing where the time goes, at low cost
items.detail_md: System traces first; only if they can't tell, an opt-in recorder whose own cost is measured, with the emulated timing left as it is.

items.title: Measuring a frame's copies on its way to the screen
items.detail_md: Each step from the N64's video output to the window timed on its own, waits included; what it would gain is unknown.

items.title: Counting the N64's waits for its graphics
items.detail_md: How often and how long it waits, timed against the GPU, with every wait kept in place.

items.title: A clearer view of frame pacing
items.detail_md: Each frame's time split into sleeping, waiting, running and presenting, since frames per second alone isn't enough.

items.title: Measuring what the sound path costs
items.detail_md: Its allocations, lock time and dropouts measured before any change to its buffers, as an experiment that runs only if I approve it.

items.title: More of the N64's RSP vector code in NEON
items.detail_md: Two parts have merged; next, checking the code as built and the RSP's share of the CPU, then the other frequent vector instructions.

items.title: Measuring the N64's video modes and fallbacks
items.detail_md: Counting mode changes, fallback frames and each mode's cost, with Mario Tennis and Rogue Squadron kept as regression checks.

items.title: Measuring the N64's recompiler and data cache
items.detail_md: Sampling block exits, invalidations, cache activity and CPU share, with the sampling's own cost measured.

items.title: Profiling the other systems
items.detail_md: The PlayStation, Super Famicom, Game Boy Advance, Mega Drive and others, profiled before any new recompiler or renderer.

items.title: Several controllers at once
items.detail_md: Each controller on a port of its own, with its own input and rumble.

items.title: The N64's true frame rate in the performance monitor
items.detail_md: The frames a game draws, told apart from the rate the video signal scans out.

items.title: ZX Spectrum: tape swapping and a picker for ZIPs
items.detail_md: Swapping between a game's tapes, and choosing the file to load from a ZIP that holds several.

items.title: Dynamic speed compensation
items.detail_md: Scaling the emulated clock and sound to smooth games that run slow: a question of accuracy, not a speed-up.

items.title: Run-ahead, on systems other than the N64
items.detail_md: It needs each frame saved, run unseen and restored, which isn't practical on the N64; its switch stays hidden till then.

items.title: A libretro host, for established emulators
items.detail_md: Parked: the emulators it would host are under the GPL, and the firmware ares ships, which I'm keeping, can't be.

items.title: Dreamcast, NAOMI and Atomiswave
items.detail_md: Planned through Flycast, a GPL emulator, so it's parked while I keep the firmware ares ships.

items.title: The Saturn, eventually
items.detail_md: The recommended route is Mednafen's emulator, the most accurate open one, under the GPL; a core of Phobos's own would take years.

items.title: Nintendo DS
items.detail_md: Suggested rather than asked for: melonDS, under the GPL, with two-screen layouts and touch on the lower screen.

items.title: Arcade boards beyond the Neo Geo
items.detail_md: CPS-1 and CPS-2 first, then Sega's System 16 and 18 and CPS-3, ported from MAME's drivers in ares's style.

items.title: Smaller consoles and handhelds
items.detail_md: The Atari 7800, Lynx, 5200 and Jaguar, Virtual Boy, Intellivision, Vectrex, Sega Pico, 3DO, PC-FX, Odyssey², Pokémon Mini and Game & Watch, one task each.

items.title: Retro computers
items.detail_md: The Commodore 64, Amiga, Amstrad CPC, Atari ST, DOS, MSX2+ and turbo R, with on-screen and physical keyboards; lower priority.

items.title: Automatic PSP speed comparisons
items.detail_md: Comparing the PSP core's speed by script, built on the reproducible PSP runs that have merged.

items.title: Tests for the PSP's pictures above 1x on Vulkan
items.detail_md: Guarding high-resolution Vulkan output; two of the core's parts already test some frames above 1x.

items.title: No more timing-sensitive thread tests
items.detail_md: Taking out the thread tests whose result depends on timing.

items.title: Tests that old PSP save states still load
items.detail_md: Checking save states from earlier versions, once their layout settles.

items.title: Measuring the real Android graphics driver
items.detail_md: On my RP6, after the automatic speed comparisons and the high-resolution tests.

items.title: More replayable tests of the PSP's recompiler
items.detail_md: More tests that replay code through the recompiler and check it against a reference.

items.title: Keeping the tests of the PSP's dialogs
items.detail_md: Tests of answering the PSP's system dialogs, its messages, keyboard and saves, kept in the suite.

items.title: Tests that settings and controls are kept
items.detail_md: Making sure a change can't lose the settings and controls you've chosen.

items.title: Tests of the Android app's launch and storage
items.detail_md: Covering how the app starts and how it uses storage.

items.title: Tests that saves fail safely
items.detail_md: A shared helper for writing saves first, then tests of what happens when a write fails.

items.title: Fuzzing the PSP core's inputs
items.detail_md: Random and edge-case input fed to the PSP core at its boundaries, to find what breaks it.

items.title: Tests of the files each APK update relies on
items.detail_md: Checking that each build's update files are what the app's updater expects.

items.title: Smoke tests of the packaged desktop builds
items.detail_md: Checking that the AppImage, the Windows build and the macOS app start, as they ship.

items.title: Tests guarding the N64's Vulkan lifecycle
items.detail_md: Not now: there's no way to test it short of a redesign.

items.title: The old CPU test harnesses restored
items.detail_md: Not now: they test cores nobody is changing.

items.title: Measuring test coverage honestly
items.detail_md: How much of the code the tests reach, counted without inflating it.

items.title: Automating the evidence each change needs
items.detail_md: Collecting the evidence for each change's review automatically.

items.title: A fresh Neo Geo compatibility pass
items.detail_md: A bounded pass over the games, since the fixes so far don't prove that every set works.

items.title: Shaders and a responsive layout
items.detail_md: Kept for later: shaders that apply in a game (the Shaders screen saves a preset but doesn't apply it yet), the polish around them, and a layout that adapts to the screen.

items.title: A proper bypass of the N64's data cache
items.detail_md: Parked as high-risk: a first, direct version broke the console's memory transfers, so it needs a sound design.

items.title: Per-game timing and cache overrides
items.detail_md: Parked until a measured need shows up, and then only with a review of the timing.

items.title: A recompiler for the PlayStation's CPU
items.detail_md: Wanted eventually, after profiling, with the interpreter kept as a fallback.

items.title: PlayStation graphics off the CPU
items.detail_md: Wanted eventually, in two parts: the simpler pixel copying, measured, then the riskier renderer.

items.title: A recompiler for the Super Famicom's CPU
items.detail_md: Profiling comes first.

items.title: A recompiler for the Game Boy Advance's CPU
items.detail_md: Profiling comes first.

items.title: A faster, optional take on the Mega Drive's video chip
items.detail_md: Wanted eventually, behind a setting of its own, after a review of its compatibility.

items.title: Accuracy or speed by default, on four systems
items.detail_md: Measuring what the accurate modes cost on my RP6, then choosing the defaults for the Super Famicom, PC Engine, Game Boy Advance and WonderSwan.

items.title: More opt-in speed options for the N64
items.detail_md: Each measured on my RP6 first: skipping idle loops at normal speed, automatic frame skip and keeping the GPU's clock up, among others.

items.title: A recompiler for the ZX Spectrum's CPU
items.detail_md: Probably not needed, and profiling comes first.

items.title: MSX tapes: the load command typed for you
items.detail_md: Not done yet: for now you type the command that loads a tape yourself.

items.title: A Super Mario 64 hack that stops at boot
items.detail_md: B3313's v1.0.2 Hotfix 3 stays on a black screen; the first suspect is the N64 CPU's timer, which Phobos does differently from ares.

items.title: F-Zero ZX Overdrive's black picture
items.detail_md: It runs at full speed with steady sound, but its picture stays black, apart from a few dots.

items.title: A README that shows what Phobos does
items.detail_md: The GitHub page rewritten with current screenshots, and what's outdated there replaced; not a priority yet.

items.title: Box art and game details in the Library
items.detail_md: An optional grid of box art, with each game's title, year, publisher and description, from a source whose terms allow it.

items.title: Live switching for the PSP
items.detail_md: Changing the PSP's resolution and renderer mid-game, with no restart. The GE work it was waiting on has merged now.

items.title: Vulkan (accurate), faster
items.detail_md: Getting the accurate Vulkan renderer closer to the fast one's speed on the handheld.

items.title: Custom colour schemes
items.detail_md: Colour schemes of your own, beside the 13 themes.
